title: 10-Year Treasury Note auction — the November refunding NEW issue, 1:00pm ET, the same session as the October CPI print and the last bond session before the Veterans Day closure
source: EST: treasury.gov Tentative Schedule of Treasury Auctions PDF (home.treasury.gov/system/files/221/Tentative-Auction-Schedule.pdf), re-fetched direct by plain curl 2026-09-09 (HTTP 200, 17,195 bytes) and its text layer decompressed stream-by-stream by THIS session, independently of the proposal that discovered it. Row reads verbatim `10-Year NOTE / Wednesday, November 04, 2026 / Tuesday, November 10, 2026 / Monday, November 16, 2026` — no trailing `R`, so a NEW ISSUE, announced by the 2026-11-04 quarterly refunding statement. The same PDF carries its own line `Holiday - Wednesday, November 11, 2026 - Veterans Day`, a Treasury primary for the closure this auction sits immediately in front of. Settlement is Monday 11-16 because the customary 15th is a Sunday; the note will be dated 2026-11-15 and back-dated, first coupon 2027-05-15. 1:00pm ET is Treasury's standing coupon-auction convention and is NOT separately sourced. Filed estimate on the two limits this lane records: a tentative schedule is tentative by construction, and this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep. Checked 2026-09-09
notes: CANONICAL FILE WRITTEN 2026-09-09 by this event's own never-assessed initial research, which read `proposals/treasury-10y-note-2026-11-10.from-treasury-30y-bond-2026-11-12.json` in full first (EVENT-RESEARCH.md). ONE CORRECTION TO THAT PROPOSAL, primary-derived and in the conservative direction: the proposal put the expected size at $42B on a streak dated from 2025-02-12 (7 auctions). The streak is longer — `auctions_query` pulled 2026-09-09, TIPS excluded by a non-null `ref_cpi_on_issue_date`, shows ELEVEN consecutive nominal 10-Year new issues at $42B from 2024-02-07 through 2026-08-12, across clearing yields 3.960% to 4.683%. The size claim is stronger than proposed, not weaker. THE ONE THING GENUINELY NEW HERE, and it is a first: in the 18 November 10-Year auctions on record (2009-2025) the October-data CPI has NEVER shared the auction's session — it landed a median 7-8 days later, closest being the NEXT day in 2021 and 2022. 2026-11-10 is the first collision, because two independent calendar mechanics meet: BLS moved the October-data CPI to Tuesday 2026-11-10 08:30 ET (confirmed, bls.gov/schedule/news_release/cpi.htm, re-read 2026-09-09) and Veterans Day falling on a Wednesday pushes the 10-Year leg to Tuesday. THE COMBINATION IS UNPRECEDENTED; EVERY COMPONENT IS ORDINARY, and each was measured this session. (1) A 10-Year auction sharing a session with CPI has happened 30 times since 2018; against each one's four nearest non-CPI 10-Year auctions the bid-to-cover delta is +0.004 and the indirect share is +2.75pp — no demand penalty, a mild tilt toward end investors. (2) The Tuesday-Nov-10 slot with a shut Wednesday behind it is 3/3: 2009-11-10, 2015-11-10 and 2020-11-10 were all 10-Year NEW issues on exactly this date, bid-to-cover 2.570 against 2.506 for the other twelve Novembers. (3) The 10-Year yield's move from those auction closes across the closure to the next session was -5, 0 and -10bp, mean absolute 5.7bp against 4.6bp for ordinary next-day rolls, max 10bp against 30bp — no precedent for a large adverse gap. HEADLINE SUPPLY UNDERSTATES THE LINE BY ~$11B: 15/15 nominal 10-Year new issues since 2023 took a positive SOMA add-on; on the $42B era it has run $6.54B-$14.83B, mean $11.38B, accepted/offering 1.271x, so 2026-08-12 offered $42B and accepted $52.62B. THE 10-YEAR IS THE ONLY AUCTION ON 11-10 per the tentative schedule — the session's bills are announcements (4-, 8- and 17-week, auctioned 11-12) and settlements, so the 1:00pm print is the session's sole Treasury supply event. Size is NOT published today (sb0590's anticipated-size table ends at Oct-26) and becomes published 2026-11-04. Read it, do not trade it: `symbols: []`, date is `estimate`, and no house playbook (S1/S2/E1/S3/S4 + G1) is rates-keyed.
